BOUT REVIEW

Last bout

How the Gauntlet works
  • There are four groups of four. Every member takes one turn alone against the other three. Group winners advance and rotate through one more round of roles in the final.
  • The solo fighter must defeat the entire trio. The trio wins by defeating the solo fighter. Clock expiry is a draw; it does not become a win based on damage or survivors.
  • Elo compares the solo fighter with the trio’s combined rating. Four equal-rated fighters give the solo side a 25% expected score. The solo fighter takes the full signed Elo change; the trio splits the opposite change. The 1500 floor applies to everyone.
  • Mastery badges follow your peak Elo after a rated bout: GM 1500, HGM 1600, SGM 1700, AGM 1800.
  • Final standings use solo points, then total points, then the initial seed. If all four final bouts draw, no champion or medals are awarded.
  • Role results train each fighter separately. The career ledger records current and peak Elo across seasons. Gauntlet progress stays in this browser; use Manage saves to move it to another device.
